title: A bounded planet-period error gives less than 0.938 m/s of the early GJ 3341 residual
abstract: We test whether an error in the fixed period of GJ 3341 b can produce a prior 15.052-day residual in 61 early HARPS visits. A linear projection bound gives at most 0.937732 m/s for any period from 14.186 to 14.228 days, fundamental amplitude at most 5 m/s, and first harmonic amplitude at most 2 m/s. The fitted residual amplitude is 2.262251 m/s. A wider variable-period fit leaves 2.375233 m/s. Direct fits, random phase trials, and a derivative bound check the result. The bound covers period error alone in a two-harmonic waveform. Noise, activity, higher harmonics, and shared instrument errors remain possible. The extra period was selected in prior work on these data. No new planet, signal significance, or independent telescope confirmation is reported. Code, raw snapshot, source hashes, tables, figure, proof, and offline instructions are included.

display.caption: Early error profiles and a bound on period-error leakage. The bound assumes a fundamental amplitude at most 5 m/s and first harmonic at most 2 m/s. Noise is outside the bound.
